## Fig. 1A
```{r}

world <- giscoR::gisco_get_countries(resolution = "10")

metadata <- metadata %>% 
  mutate(Origin = recode(Geographical_origin,
                         "USA"                    = "United States",
                         "UK"                     = "United Kingdom",
                         "USA"                    = "United States",
                         "South_Africa"           = "South Africa",
                         "New_Zealand"            = "New Zealand",
                         "Bosnia_and_Herzegovina" = "Bosnia and Herzegovina",
                         "HongKong_China"         = "Hong Kong"))

meta_counts <- metadata %>%
  group_by(Origin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

world_meta <- world %>%
  left_join(meta_counts, by = c("NAME_ENGL" = "Origin"))

map_plot <- ggplot(world_meta) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = n)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "grey90") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  labs(fill = "Sample Count",
       title = "Countries represented in metadata")

print(map_plot)

bar_plot <- ggplot(meta_counts, aes(x = reorder(Origin, -n), y = n, fill = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "", y = "N° of samples", title = "") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "grey90") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x    = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.title    = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(bar_plot)

```

## Fig. 2A
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(vegan)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
library(ggsignif)
library(rstatix)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(svglite)
library(gtsummary)
library(flextable)
library(writexl)
library(glue)
library(tibble)

alpha_Kefir <- read.table("../../data/alpha_diversity_Kefir.csv",
                          header = TRUE,
                          sep = ",",
                          check.names = FALSE,
                          comment.char = "",
                          quote = "",
                          na = ""
                          ) %>% as.data.frame()

unique(alpha_Kefir$Subtype)
Subtype <- c(
  "Water_kefir" = "steelblue",
  "Milk_kefir"  = "#FFC857"
)

# Simpson
simpson_subtype <- ggbetweenstats(
  data               = alpha_Kefir,
  x                  = Subtype,
  y                  = Simpson,
  type               = 'nonparametric',
  test               = 'wilcox.test',
  
  # Pairwise comparisons
  pairwise.comparisons = TRUE,
  pairwise.annotation  = 'p.value',
  pairwise.display     = 'all',
  p.adjust.method      = 'fdr',
  
  # Subtitle & descriptives
  results.subtitle     = TRUE,
  sample.size.label    = TRUE,
  mean.plotting        = TRUE,
  mean.ci              = TRUE,
  
  # Boxplot / violin / stats aesthetics
  centrality.point.args = list(size = 0, color = 'darkred'),
  centrality.label.args = list(label = NA,
                               size = 3,
                               nudge_x = 0.4,
                               segment.linetype   = 4,
                               min.segment.length = 0),
  point.args           = list(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.5),
                              alpha = 0.75, size = 2, stroke = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
  boxplot.args         = list(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE),
  violin.args          = list(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
  ggsignif.args        = list(textsize = 3, tip_length = 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
  
  ggtheme              = theme_ggstatsplot(),
  package              = 'awtools',
  palette              = 'bpalette'
) +
  scale_color_manual(values = Subtype) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = Subtype) +
  theme(
    axis.ticks         = element_blank(),
    axis.line          = element_line(colour = 'grey50'),
    panel.grid         = element_line(color  = '#b4aea9'),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = 'dashed')
  )

# Extract statistics calculated by ggstatsplot
ggstats <- ggstatsplot::extract_stats(simpson_subtype)

# Extract ggstatsplot p-value
p_ggstats <- ggstats$subtitle_data$p.value

# Create significance label from ggstatsplot p-value
p_label <- dplyr::case_when(
  p_ggstats <= 0.0001 ~ "****",
  p_ggstats <= 0.001  ~ "***",
  p_ggstats <= 0.01   ~ "**",
  p_ggstats <= 0.05   ~ "*",
  TRUE                ~ "ns"
)

# Define y-position for bracket
y_max <- max(alpha_Kefir$Simpson, na.rm = TRUE)
y_min <- min(alpha_Kefir$Simpson, na.rm = TRUE)
y_range <- y_max - y_min

# Final plot with ggstatsplot p-value added as bracket annotation
simpson_subtype_sig <- simpson_subtype +
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(c("Water_kefir", "Milk_kefir")),
    annotations = p_label,
    manual = FALSE,
    textsize = 3,
    tip_length = 0.01,
    y_position = y_max + 0.10 * y_range
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(y_min, y_max + 0.25 * y_range),
    clip = "off"
  )

simpson_subtype_sig


# Shannon
shannon_subtype <- ggbetweenstats(
  data               = alpha_Kefir,
  x                  = Subtype,
  y                  = Shannon,
  type               = 'nonparametric',
  test               = 'wilcox.test',
  
  # Pairwise comparisons
  pairwise.comparisons = TRUE,
  pairwise.annotation  = 'p.value',
  pairwise.display     = 'all',
  p.adjust.method      = 'fdr',
  
  # Subtitle & descriptives
  results.subtitle     = TRUE,
  sample.size.label    = TRUE,
  mean.plotting        = TRUE,
  mean.ci              = TRUE,
  
  # Boxplot / violin / stats aesthetics
  centrality.point.args = list(size = 0, color = 'darkred'),
  centrality.label.args = list(label = NA,
                               size = 3,
                               nudge_x = 0.4,
                               segment.linetype   = 4,
                               min.segment.length = 0),
  point.args           = list(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.5),
                              alpha = 0.75, size = 2, stroke = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
  boxplot.args         = list(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE),
  violin.args          = list(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
  ggsignif.args        = list(textsize = 3, tip_length = 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
  
  ggtheme              = theme_ggstatsplot(),
  package              = 'awtools',
  palette              = 'bpalette'
) +
  scale_color_manual(values = Subtype) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = Subtype) +
  theme(
    axis.ticks         = element_blank(),
    axis.line          = element_line(colour = 'grey50'),
    panel.grid         = element_line(color  = '#b4aea9'),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = 'dashed')
  )

# Extract statistics calculated by ggstatsplot
ggstats <- ggstatsplot::extract_stats(shannon_subtype)

# Extract ggstatsplot p-value
p_ggstats <- ggstats$subtitle_data$p.value

# Create significance label from ggstatsplot p-value
p_label <- dplyr::case_when(
  p_ggstats <= 0.0001 ~ "****",
  p_ggstats <= 0.001  ~ "***",
  p_ggstats <= 0.01   ~ "**",
  p_ggstats <= 0.05   ~ "*",
  TRUE                ~ "ns"
)

# Define y-position for bracket
y_max <- max(alpha_Kefir$Shannon, na.rm = TRUE)
y_min <- min(alpha_Kefir$Shannon, na.rm = TRUE)
y_range <- y_max - y_min

# Final plot with ggstatsplot p-value added as bracket annotation
shannon_subtype_sig <- shannon_subtype +
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(c("Water_kefir", "Milk_kefir")),
    annotations = p_label,
    manual = FALSE,
    textsize = 3,
    tip_length = 0.01,
    y_position = y_max + 0.10 * y_range
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(y_min, y_max + 0.25 * y_range),
    clip = "off"
  )

shannon_subtype_sig


# Pielou's Evenness
pielou_subtype <- ggbetweenstats(
  data               = alpha_Kefir,
  x                  = Subtype,
  y                  = Pielou,
  type               = 'nonparametric',
  test               = 'wilcox.test',
  
  # Pairwise comparisons
  pairwise.comparisons = TRUE,
  pairwise.annotation  = 'p.value',
  pairwise.display     = 'all',
  p.adjust.method      = 'fdr',
  
  # Subtitle & descriptives
  results.subtitle     = TRUE,

  mean.plotting        = TRUE,
  mean.ci              = TRUE,
  
  # Boxplot / violin / stats aesthetics
  centrality.point.args = list(size = 0, color = 'darkred'),

  point.args           = list(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.5),

  boxplot.args         = list(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE),
  violin.args          = list(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),

  ggtheme              = theme_ggstatsplot(),

  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = Subtype) +

    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
```

## Fig. 2B
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggrepel)
library(grid)
library(patchwork)
library(vegan)
library(ape)
library(Rtsne)

s_metaKefir <- read.table("s_metaKefir.tsv",
                      header       = TRUE,
                      row.names    = 1,
                      sep          = "\t",
                      check.names  = FALSE,
                      dec          = ".",
                      comment.char = "",
                      quote        = ""
                      ) %>% as.data.frame() 

dim(s_metaKefir)
head(s_metaKefir)

s_metaKefir <- s_metaKefir %>% 
  filter(Liquid_OR_Grain == "Liquid")

# In this table, species columns start with "s__"
species_cols <- grep("^s__", colnames(s_metaKefir), value = TRUE)

if (length(species_cols) == 0) {
  stop("No species columns found. Expected columns starting with 's__'.")
}

meta_cols <- setdiff(colnames(s_metaKefir), species_cols)

taxa_pcoa <- s_metaKefir[, species_cols, drop = FALSE]
meta_pcoa <- s_metaKefir[, meta_cols,    drop = FALSE]

cat("Metadata columns: ", length(meta_cols), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Species columns: ",  length(species_cols), "\n", sep = "")

# Convert species abundance table to numeric matrix
taxa_pcoa <- taxa_pcoa %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(taxa_pcoa) <- rownames(s_metaKefir)
rownames(meta_pcoa) <- rownames(s_metaKefir)

taxa_pcoa <- as.matrix(taxa_pcoa)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Clean abundance table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Replace NA, NaN and Inf values with 0
non_finite_values <- !is.finite(taxa_pcoa)

if (any(non_finite_values)) {
  cat("Warning: ", sum(non_finite_values),
      " non-finite values in taxa table — replacing with 0\n", sep = "")
  taxa_pcoa[non_finite_values] <- 0
}

# Diagnostic checks
cat("NA values in taxa_pcoa: ",  sum(is.na(taxa_pcoa)), "\n",
    "NaN values in taxa_pcoa: ", sum(is.nan(taxa_pcoa)), "\n",
    "Inf values in taxa_pcoa: ", sum(is.infinite(taxa_pcoa)), "\n",
    "Negative values in taxa_pcoa: ", sum(taxa_pcoa < 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n",
    sep = "")

if (any(taxa_pcoa < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  stop("Negative values found in taxa_pcoa. Bray-Curtis requires non-negative abundances.")
}

# Drop species that are zero across all samples
nonzero_species <- colSums(taxa_pcoa) > 0

cat("Species retained before sample filtering: ",
    sum(nonzero_species), " of ", length(nonzero_species), "\n", sep = "")

taxa_pcoa <- taxa_pcoa[, nonzero_species, drop = FALSE]

# Check per-sample row sums
sample_sums <- rowSums(taxa_pcoa)

cat("Samples with row sum = 0: ", sum(sample_sums == 0), "\n",
    "Samples with row sum > 0: ", sum(sample_sums > 0), "\n",
    "Min row sum: ", min(sample_sums), "\n",
    "Max row sum: ", max(sample_sums), "\n",
    sep = "")

zero_sum_samples <- rownames(taxa_pcoa)[sample_sums == 0]

if (length(zero_sum_samples) > 0) {
  cat("\nZero-sum samples removed (", length(zero_sum_samples), "):\n", sep = "")
  print(zero_sum_samples)
}

# Drop zero-sum samples
keep_samples <- sample_sums > 0

cat("\nDropping ", sum(!keep_samples),
    " zero-sum samples; keeping ", sum(keep_samples), "\n", sep = "")

taxa_pcoa <- taxa_pcoa[keep_samples, , drop = FALSE]
meta_pcoa <- meta_pcoa[keep_samples, , drop = FALSE]

# Drop species that became zero after sample filtering
species_keep <- colSums(taxa_pcoa) > 0
taxa_pcoa   <- taxa_pcoa[, species_keep, drop = FALSE]

cat("After cleanup: ", nrow(taxa_pcoa), " samples × ",
    ncol(taxa_pcoa), " species\n", sep = "")

if (nrow(taxa_pcoa) < 3) {
  stop("Fewer than 3 samples remain after filtering. PCoA is not reliable.")
}

if (ncol(taxa_pcoa) < 2) {
  stop("Fewer than 2 species remain after filtering. Bray-Curtis PCoA is not useful.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: Bray-Curtis distance and PCoA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

bray_dist <- vegan::vegdist(taxa_pcoa, method = "bray")

n_na  <- sum(is.na(bray_dist))
n_nan <- sum(is.nan(bray_dist))
n_inf <- sum(is.infinite(bray_dist))

cat("\nDistance matrix — NA: ", n_na,
    ", NaN: ", n_nan,
    ", Inf: ", n_inf, "\n", sep = "")

stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.vector(bray_dist))))
cat("Distance matrix is clean: all values are finite.\n")

# Run PCoA
pcoa_result <- ape::pcoa(bray_dist)

# Percent variance explained
pct_var <- round(pcoa_result$values$Relative_eig * 100, 1)

cat("Variance explained — PC1: ", pct_var[1],
    "%, PC2: ", pct_var[2], "%\n", sep = "")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: Build plotting data frame
# ------------------------------------------------------------

site_scores <- as.data.frame(
  pcoa_result$vectors[, 1:min(3, ncol(pcoa_result$vectors)), drop = FALSE]
)

colnames(site_scores) <- paste0("PC", seq_len(ncol(site_scores)))

pcoa_df <- site_scores %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  left_join(
    meta_pcoa %>% rownames_to_column("SampleID"),
    by = "SampleID"
  )

cat("PCoA data frame: ", nrow(pcoa_df), " samples\n", sep = "")

# ============================================================
# Step 6: Kefir metadata palettes
# ============================================================

kefir_palettes <- list(
  
  Subtype = c(
    "Water_kefir" = "steelblue",
    "Milk_kefir"  = "#FFC857"
  ),
  
  Liquid_OR_Grain = c(
    "Liquid" = "#E4572E",

  ),
  
  Sugar_source = c(

  ),
  
  Type_of_fermentation = c(

  ),
  
  Timepoint = c(

    "2"  = "#FDBB84",
    "4"  = "#FC8D59",
    "8"  = "#E34A33",
    "16" = "#B30000",
    "24" = "#800000",

  ),
  
  Fermentation_duration = c(
    "8"  = "#A1D99B",

    "NA" = "lightgrey"
  ),
  
  Fermentation_cycle = c(

  ),

  ),

# ============================================================
# Step 7: Helper functions for safe metadata plotting
# ============================================================

# Convert true missing values to the character level "NA".
# This is important because your palettes use "NA" = "lightgrey".
clean_metadata_level <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "NaN" | x == "nan" | x == "<NA>"] <- "NA"
  x
}


# Build a safe palette for the selected metadata variable.
# If unexpected levels are present in the data, the function adds colours automatically.
make_safe_palette <- function(metadata_variable, observed_values, palette_list) {
  
  observed_values <- clean_metadata_level(observed_values)
  observed_levels <- unique(observed_values)
  
  if (!metadata_variable %in% names(palette_list)) {
    
    warning("No predefined palette found for ", metadata_variable,
            ". Using automatic colours.")
    
    auto_palette <- setNames(
      scales::hue_pal()(length(observed_levels)),
      observed_levels
    )
    
    return(auto_palette)
  }
  
  manual_palette <- palette_list[[metadata_variable]]
  
  missing_levels <- setdiff(observed_levels, names(manual_palette))
  
  if (length(missing_levels) > 0) {
    
    warning(
      "The following levels of ", metadata_variable,
      " are not present in the manual palette and will receive automatic colours: ",
      paste(missing_levels, collapse = ", ")
    )
    
    extra_palette <- setNames(
      scales::hue_pal()(length(missing_levels)),
      missing_levels
    )
    
    manual_palette <- c(manual_palette, extra_palette)
  }
  
  # Keep only levels that are actually present in the data
  manual_palette <- manual_palette[names(manual_palette) %in% observed_levels]
  
  return(manual_palette)
}

# ============================================================
# Step 8: Choose metadata variable for colouring
# ============================================================

# Change this line depending on the biological question:
# "Subtype"
# "Liquid_OR_Grain"
# "Sugar_source"
# "Type_of_fermentation"
# "Timepoint"
# "Fermentation_duration"
# "Fermentation_cycle"
# "Temperature"
# "Private_OR_Commercial"
# "Shipping_methods"
# "Geographical_origin"

plot_colour <- "Subtype"

if (!plot_colour %in% colnames(pcoa_df)) {
  stop("The selected plot_colour column was not found in pcoa_df: ", plot_colour)
}

pcoa_df <- pcoa_df %>%
  mutate(
    plot_group = clean_metadata_level(.data[[plot_colour]])
  )

plot_palette <- make_safe_palette(
  metadata_variable = plot_colour,
  observed_values   = pcoa_df$plot_group,
  palette_list      = kefir_palettes
)

# Keep factor order according to your palette
pcoa_df$plot_group <- factor(
  pcoa_df$plot_group,
  levels = names(plot_palette)
)

cat("PCoA coloured by: ", plot_colour, "\n", sep = "")
cat("Groups shown: ", paste(levels(pcoa_df$plot_group), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

# ============================================================
# Step 9: PCoA plot with your kefir palette
# ============================================================


fig_pcoa_kefir <- ggplot(

) +

  ) +

  ) +

  )

fig_pcoa_kefir

ggsave(

)

# ============================================================
# Step 10: Weighted-average species overlay
# ============================================================

wa_scores <- vegan::wascores(
  pcoa_result$vectors[, 1:2, drop = FALSE],

) %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "species") %>%
  rename(PC1 = Axis.1, PC2 = Axis.2) %>%

    species_label = gsub("^s__", "", species)
  )

species_of_interest <- c(

wa_subset <- wa_scores %>%
  filter(species_label %in% species_of_interest)

cat("Species found and labelled: ", nrow(wa_subset), " of ",
    length(species_of_interest), "\n", sep = "")

if (nrow(wa_subset) < length(species_of_interest)) {

      paste(setdiff(species_of_interest, wa_subset$species_label),
            collapse = ", "),

}

if (requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) {
  
  fig_pcoa_kefir_species <- fig_pcoa_kefir +

} else {

fig_pcoa_kefir_species

# ---- 1. Compute betadisper ----
# Reorder metadata to exactly match the sample order in bray_dist.
meta_for_disp <- meta_pcoa %>%
  rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
  filter(SampleID %in% labels(bray_dist)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("SampleID")

meta_for_disp <- meta_for_disp[labels(bray_dist), , drop = FALSE]

# Keep only samples with a valid Subtype (not NA and not an empty string).
valid_idx <- !is.na(meta_for_disp$Subtype) &
             meta_for_disp$Subtype != ""

cat(
  "Samples with valid Subtype: ",
  sum(valid_idx), " / ", length(valid_idx), "\n",
  sep = ""
)

bray_dist_valid <- as.dist(as.matrix(bray_dist)[valid_idx, valid_idx])
meta_valid      <- meta_for_disp[valid_idx, , drop = FALSE]

bray_disp <- vegan::betadisper(
  bray_dist_valid,
  group = meta_valid$Subtype,
  type  = "median"
)

# ---- 2. Build the PERMDISP data frame ----
disp_distances <- bray_disp$distances

permdisp_df_bray <- data.frame(
  Subtype          = meta_valid$Subtype,
  DistanceToMedian = disp_distances,
  row.names        = NULL,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Use the existing kefir palette for Subtype.
subtype_palette <- kefir_palettes[["Subtype"]]
permdisp_df_bray$color_id <- subtype_palette[permdisp_df_bray$Subtype]
permdisp_df_bray$color_id[is.na(permdisp_df_bray$color_id)] <- "grey50"
my_col_individual <- setNames(
  permdisp_df_bray$color_id,
  permdisp_df_bray$Subtype
)

# ---- 3. Pairwise Wilcoxon tests with FDR correction ----
permdisp_wilcox_df_bray <- permdisp_df_bray %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Subtype),
    !is.na(DistanceToMedian)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Subtype) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  droplevels()

if (n_distinct(permdisp_wilcox_df_bray$Subtype) >= 2) {

  pairwise_results_bray <- permdisp_wilcox_df_bray %>%
    rstatix::wilcox_test(DistanceToMedian ~ Subtype) %>%
    rstatix::adjust_pvalue(method = "fdr") %>%
    rstatix::add_significance(
      p.col     = "p.adj",
      cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
      symbols   = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns")
    ) %>%
    filter(p.adj.signif != "ns")

} else {

  pairwise_results_bray <- tibble()
  cat(
    "Pairwise Wilcoxon tests skipped: fewer than 2 subtypes ",
    "with at least 2 observations.\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}

max_y_bray <- max(permdisp_df_bray$DistanceToMedian, na.rm = TRUE)

if (nrow(pairwise_results_bray) > 0) {

  pairwise_results_bray <- pairwise_results_bray %>%
    mutate(
      y.position = max_y_bray + row_number() * max_y_bray * 0.06
    )

  cat(
    "Significant pairwise Wilcoxon comparisons retained: ",
    nrow(pairwise_results_bray), "\n",
    sep = ""
  )

} else {

  cat("No significant pairwise Wilcoxon comparisons to annotate.\n")
}

# ---- 4. PERMDISP plot (corrected colour mapping) ----
# Make Subtype a factor with the order from the palette
permdisp_df_bray$Subtype <- factor(permdisp_df_bray$Subtype,
                                   levels = names(subtype_palette))

fig_permdisp_subtype_bray <- ggplot(permdisp_df_bray,
                                    aes(x = Subtype,
                                        y = DistanceToMedian,
                                        colour = Subtype)) +   # <-- map to Subtype, not color_id
  geom_jitter(width = 0.18,
              size  = 2,
              alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group = Subtype),
               colour        = 'black',
               fill          = NA,
               outlier.shape = NA,
               linewidth     = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = subtype_palette,   # <-- direct use of the palette
                     name   = 'Subtype') +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x     = 'Subtype',
    y     = 'Dispersion'
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = 'bold', size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid    = element_line(colour = 'grey94', linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = 'right'
)

# Add significance brackets (unchanged)
if (nrow(pairwise_results_bray) > 0) {
  fig_permdisp_subtype_bray <- fig_permdisp_subtype_bray +
    stat_pvalue_manual(
      pairwise_results_bray,
      label      = 'p.adj.signif',
      xmin       = 'group1',
      xmax       = 'group2',
      y.position = 'y.position',
      tip.length = 0.01,
      size       = 4,
      colour     = 'black',
      hide.ns    = TRUE
    )
}

fig_permdisp_subtype_bray
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# t‑SNE on Bray‑Curtis distances — reusing the distance matrix
# ============================================================

# ---- 1. Sanity check for perplexity ----
n_samp <- attr(bray_dist, "Size")
cat("Samples for t‑SNE: ", n_samp, "\n", sep = "")

perplexity_val <- 30                 # standard default; valid for n ≥ 91
max_perp_ok    <- floor((n_samp - 1) / 3)

if (perplexity_val > max_perp_ok) {
  warning("Perplexity ", perplexity_val,
          " exceeds Rtsne limit (", max_perp_ok,
          ") for this n_samp. Lowering automatically.")
  perplexity_val <- max_perp_ok
}
cat("Perplexity: ", perplexity_val, "\n", sep = "")


# ---- 2. PCoA initialisation ----
# Initialising from PCoA coordinates gives reproducible embeddings.
mds_init <- pcoa_result$vectors[, 1:2]

# Avoid division by zero if all coordinates happen to be zero
max_abs <- max(abs(mds_init))
if (max_abs == 0) {
  warning("PCoA coordinates are all zero — using random initialisation.")
  mds_init <- NULL
} else {
  mds_init <- mds_init / max_abs * 0.0001
}


# ---- 3. Run t‑SNE ----
set.seed(123)
tsne_out <- Rtsne(
  X                = as.matrix(bray_dist),
  is_distance      = TRUE,
  perplexity       = perplexity_val,
  check_duplicates = FALSE,
  verbose          = TRUE,
  max_iter         = 1000,
  Y_init           = mds_init,
  pca              = FALSE
)

cat("t‑SNE complete. Output dimensions: ",
    paste(dim(tsne_out$Y), collapse = " × "), "\n", sep = "")


# ---- 4. Build plot data frame ----
tsne_df <- tibble(
  SampleID = rownames(as.matrix(bray_dist)),
  tSNE1    = tsne_out$Y[, 1],
  tSNE2    = tsne_out$Y[, 2]
) %>%
  left_join(meta_pcoa %>% rownames_to_column("SampleID"),
            by = "SampleID")

# Apply the same metadata cleaning and palette logic as the PCoA
tsne_df <- tsne_df %>%
  mutate(
    plot_group = clean_metadata_level(.data[[plot_colour]])
  )

plot_palette_tsne <- make_safe_palette(
  metadata_variable = plot_colour,
  observed_values   = tsne_df$plot_group,
  palette_list      = kefir_palettes
)

tsne_df$plot_group <- factor(tsne_df$plot_group,
                             levels = names(plot_palette_tsne))


# ---- 5. PERMANOVA using the same grouping variable ----
# Ensure we use the filtered meta_pcoa (same rows as bray_dist)
set.seed(123)
permanova_res <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ plot_group,
  data = tsne_df,
  permutations = 999
)

r2_val   <- round(permanova_res$R2[1], 3)
p_val    <- permanova_res$`Pr(>F)`[1]
pval_fmt <- ifelse(p_val < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_val))

cat("PERMANOVA: R² = ", r2_val, ", p = ", pval_fmt, "\n", sep = "")


# ---- 6. t‑SNE plot ----
fig_tsne <- ggplot(tsne_df,
                   aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2, colour = plot_group)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = plot_palette_tsne,
    name   = plot_colour,
    drop   = FALSE
  ) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("Bray‑Curtis"),
    #subtitle = bquote(R^2 == .(r2_val) * ", " ~ italic(p) == .(pval_fmt)),
    x        = "t-SNE1",
    y        = "t-SNE2"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10),
    panel.grid    = element_line(colour = "grey94", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

fig_tsne

# ---- 7. Weighted‑average species overlay ----
wa_scores_tsne <- wascores(tsne_out$Y, taxa_pcoa) %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "species") %>%
  rename(tSNE1 = V1, tSNE2 = V2) %>%
  mutate(
    # Remove MetaPhlAn species prefix
    species_label = gsub("^s__", "", species),

    # Create display label: replace underscores with spaces
    species_label_plot = gsub("_", " ", species_label)
  )

species_of_interest <- c(
  "Lactococcus_lactis",
  "Lactococcus_cremoris",
  "Streptococcus_thermophilus",
  "Lactobacillus_helveticus",
  "Lactobacillus_kefiranofaciens",
  "Lentilactobacillus_kefiri",
  "Lentilactobacillus_parakefiri",
  "Leuconostoc_mesenteroides",
  "Saccharomyces_cerevisiae",
  "Acetobacter_fabarum",
  "Acetobacter_orientalis",
  "Zymomonas_mobilis",
  "Oenococcus_oeni",
  "Bifidobacterium_aquikefiri"
)

wa_subset_tsne <- wa_scores_tsne %>%
  filter(species_label %in% species_of_interest)

cat("Species found and labelled in t‑SNE: ", nrow(wa_subset_tsne), " of ",
    length(species_of_interest), "\n", sep = "")
if (nrow(wa_subset_tsne) < length(species_of_interest)) {
  cat("Not found: ",
      paste(setdiff(species_of_interest, wa_subset_tsne$species_label),
            collapse = ", "),
      "\n", sep = "")
}

fig_tsne_species <- fig_tsne +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = wa_subset_tsne,
    aes(x = tSNE1, y = tSNE2, label = species_label_plot),
    inherit.aes   = FALSE,
    colour        = "black",
    fill          = grDevices::adjustcolor("white", alpha.f = 0.75),
    fontface      = "bold.italic",
    size          = 3.5,
    label.size    = 0.25,
    label.r       = unit(0.15, "lines"),
    label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"),
    box.padding   = 0.25,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    segment.color = "grey98"
  )

fig_tsne_species
```

```{r}
##=== 5.1 All ================= (adapted for kefir)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare data matrix (species only)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Identify species columns (starting with "s__") – same logic as in your Bray-Curtis code
species_cols <- grep("^s__", colnames(s_metaKefir_log1p), value = TRUE)

if (length(species_cols) == 0) {
  stop("No species columns found. Expected columns starting with 's__'.")
}

# Transpose: rows = species, columns = samples
s_metaKefir_heatmap <- t(as.matrix(s_metaKefir_log1p[, species_cols, drop = FALSE]))

# Remove the taxonomy prefix from displayed row labels
rownames(s_metaKefir_heatmap) <- rownames(s_metaKefir_heatmap) |>
  sub("^s__", "", x = _) |>
  gsub("_", " ", x = _)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Choose viridis palette (uncomment your favourite)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# viridis_palette <- viridis(100)        # Default viridis
viridis_palette <- magma(100)          # Magma
# viridis_palette <- plasma(100)         # Plasma
# viridis_palette <- inferno(100)        # Inferno
# viridis_palette <- cividis(100)          # Cividis (colorblind friendly)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Helper to convert missing values to "NA" for consistent colouring
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
clean_metadata_level <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "NaN" | x == "nan" | x == "<NA>"] <- "NA"
  x
}

# Apply to each annotation column (optional, but recommended)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Subtype_clean            <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Subtype)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Liquid_OR_Grain_clean    <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Liquid_OR_Grain)

s_metaKefir_log1p$Type_of_fermentation_clean <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Type_of_fermentation)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Timepoint_clean          <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Timepoint)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Fermentation_duration_clean <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Fermentation_duration)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Fermentation_cycle_clean <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Fermentation_cycle)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Temperature_clean        <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Temperature)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Private_OR_Commercial_clean <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Private_OR_Commercial)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Shipping_methods_clean   <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Shipping_methods)
s_metaKefir_log1p$Geographical_origin_clean <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Geographical_origin)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Define colour palettes (reuse kefir_palettes from your earlier script)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Make sure kefir_palettes is already defined in your environment.
# If not, paste the definition from your Bray-Curtis code here.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build heatmap annotation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Subtype            = s_metaKefir_log1p$Subtype_clean,
  #Liquid_OR_Grain    = s_metaKefir_log1p$Liquid_OR_Grain_clean,
  #Sugar_source       = s_metaKefir_log1p$Sugar_source_clean,
  #Type_of_fermentation = s_metaKefir_log1p$Type_of_fermentation_clean,
  #Timepoint          = s_metaKefir_log1p$Timepoint_clean,
  #Fermentation_duration = s_metaKefir_log1p$Fermentation_duration_clean,
  #Fermentation_cycle = s_metaKefir_log1p$Fermentation_cycle_clean,
  #Temperature        = s_metaKefir_log1p$Temperature_clean,
  #Private_OR_Commercial = s_metaKefir_log1p$Private_OR_Commercial_clean,
  #Shipping_methods   = s_metaKefir_log1p$Shipping_methods_clean,
  #Geographical_origin = s_metaKefir_log1p$Geographical_origin_clean,
  
  # Apply the colour scheme from your kefir_palettes
  col = kefir_palettes,
  
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  simple_anno_size = unit(4, "mm")
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Create heatmap
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
all_heatmap <- Heatmap(
  matrix = s_metaKefir_heatmap,
  name = "Log1p abundance\nof microbial species",
  col = viridis_palette,
  na_col = "grey90",
  
  top_annotation = ha,
  
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_method_rows = "complete",
  show_row_dend = TRUE,
  row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
  
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  border = TRUE,
  row_gap = unit(2, "mm"),
  column_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "italic"),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  
  heatmap_legend_param = list(
    title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
    legend_height = unit(4, "cm"),
    direction = "vertical",
    border = "black"
  )
)

# Display
all_heatmap

##=== 5.2 All (matrix split by Subtype) =================

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare the data matrix (species only)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
species_cols <- grep("^s__", colnames(s_metaKefir_log1p), value = TRUE)

if (length(species_cols) == 0) {
  stop("No species columns found. Expected columns starting with 's__'.")
}

# Transpose: rows = species, columns = samples
s_metaKefir_heatmap <- t(as.matrix(s_metaKefir_log1p[, species_cols, drop = FALSE]))

# Remove the taxonomy prefix from displayed row labels
rownames(s_metaKefir_heatmap) <- rownames(s_metaKefir_heatmap) |>
  sub("^s__", "", x = _) |>
  gsub("_", " ", x = _)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Ensure splitting variable is clean (no NA surprises)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use the same cleaning function as before
clean_metadata_level <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "NaN" | x == "nan" | x == "<NA>"] <- "NA"
  x
}

split_variable <- clean_metadata_level(s_metaKefir_log1p$Subtype)

# Optional: check levels
cat("Split levels: ", paste(unique(split_variable), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Reuse the same annotation object (ha) from previous heatmap
#    (Make sure 'ha' is already defined, or redefine it here)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# If ha is not yet in your environment, copy its definition from the 
# previous heatmap code (section 5.1). It uses kefir_palettes and cleaned columns.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Choose viridis palette (uncomment your favourite)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# viridis_palette <- viridis(100)
viridis_palette <- magma(100)
# viridis_palette <- plasma(100)
# viridis_palette <- inferno(100)
# viridis_palette <- cividis(100)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create split heatmap
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
all_heatmap_matrix_split <- Heatmap(
  matrix = s_metaKefir_heatmap,
  name = "Log1p abundance\nof microbial species",
  col = viridis_palette,
  na_col = "grey90",
  
  top_annotation = ha,               # same annotation as full heatmap
  
  column_split = split_variable,     # split by Subtype
  # column_title = c("Grain", "Liquid"),  # uncomment if you know the exact order
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold"),
  
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,           # columns not clustered within splits
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_method_rows = "complete",
  show_row_dend = FALSE,
  row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
  cluster_column_slices = FALSE,     # don't reorder the split groups
  
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  border = TRUE,
  row_gap = unit(2, "mm"),
  column_gap = unit(1, "mm"),
  
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "italic"),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  
  heatmap_legend_param = list(
    title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
    legend_height = unit(4, "cm"),
    direction = "vertical",
    border = "black"
  )
)

# Display
all_heatmap_matrix_split
```
